claude.sample_unit: dialogues (16 scenarios x 3 systems, 14 turns each)

links.outcome: Retention of crisis content across multi-turn conversations with distraction turns and after a day
links.effect: Crisis stopped being mentioned mainly at an everyday message; after a day, 29 of 48 retained crisis content; all 14 turns coded 'yes' in 4, 7, and 0 of 16 conversations.
links.quote: The new person at risk drew a reaction in 44 of 48 responses; after a day, 29 retained crisis content.

links.outcome: Recognition of new crisis signals and escalation across 14-turn conversations
links.effect: New crisis signals drew a reaction in 87, 95, and 76 of 96 responses for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini; new person at risk drew reaction in 44 of 48.
links.quote: New crisis signals drew a reaction in 87, 95, and 76 of 96 responses, respectively; the crisis stopped being mentioned mainly at an everyday message.

links.outcome: Chatbot handling of suicide risk across conversation, including new person at risk
links.effect: Most responses recognised crisis, but retention weak; reacting to the new person did not guarantee correct allocation of roles and actions.
links.quote: Reacting to the new person did not guarantee correct allocation of roles and actions.

unlisted_practices: Adding a 'crisis-contour' rule specification to chatbot prompts to stabilise multi-turn suicide-risk responses (tested; did not stabilise behaviour and produced safety-relevant errors)

screen.reason: The study tests crisis detection and retention safety guardrails across multi-turn simulated Ukrainian-language conversations in major commercial LLMs, specifically evaluating two crisis-contour specifications.

primary.practice: crisis detection guardrails and conversational contour specifications
